scope: Two specification-derived applications, development-only library construction, one full target per app and 12 heldout interaction sequences. Not official benchmark scores or 24 independent tasks.

libraries.design: Reusable full-page checklist GUI built as a static, directly-configurable page. The page provides an input (.new-todo), a dynamic list (.todo-list) with items that support edit-in-place, individual removal, completion toggles, bulk toggle (#toggle-all), visible item filtering via hash routes (#/, #/active, #/completed), counts, and clear-completed. The runtime is plain HTML/CSS/ES modules with no external dependencies. A data-only plan configures which capabilities are enabled and how identity and persistence work. Defaults enable all demonstrated capabilities and persistence using localStorage key todos-transfer. The components and state: - App shell: header with .new-todo; .main section containing #toggle-all and .todo-list; .footer with .todo-count strong, .filters, and .clear-completed. - Item model: { id, title, completed }. Duplicate titles are allowed; identity is stable and persisted. - Renderer: fully re-renders list based on state and current route; toggles UI visibility and selection classes; hides .main and .footer iff no items (unless feature gated off). - Editing: double-click label to enter .editing mode; shows .edit; Enter/blur commit (trimmed; empty deletes), Escape cancels; normal controls hidden while editing. - Bulk actions: #toggle-all sets all items regardless of filter; checked iff nonempty collection is all complete. - Filters: anchors update hash; route survives reload; membership updates immediately on route/data changes; selected class on active link. - Persistence: commit mutations save items (id/title/completed only) to localStorage; restored on load; editing mode and unsaved text are not persisted. - Composition: plan toggles routing, persistence, bulk actions, counts, filters, footer visibility, theme, id strategy, and storage key. The UI text is frozen; plans only change semantics and feature visibility. Limitations: - The plan schema restricts string options to a small, validated set of identifiers; no arbitrary text customization. - Identity strategies are limited to incremental or timestamp. - Single checklist instance per page.

Reusable full-page GUI library: Checklist UI assembled from composable, data-first operations over shared state. State ownership: a single application state object owns the persisted collection and ephemeral UI state. All operations are pure transformations on state followed by persistence (if configured) and a deterministic re-render. Identity invariants: each item has a unique, persistent numeric id; titles are arbitrary strings; duplicates allowed; completed is boolean. Editing mode and draft text are ephemeral and never persisted. Derived-view consistency: DOM is a pure projection of state and route. Filtered membership and control visibility update immediately when state or route changes. Operations are capability-agnostic and can be enabled/disabled by plan flags; the same operations back the minimal editor, status management, filters, and persistence in any combination.
Core components and contracts:
- State model (owned by app):
  - items: [{ id:number, title:string, completed:boolean }]
  - nextId:number (1 + max(id) after restore; starts at 1 when empty)
  - route: 'all' | 'active' | 'completed' (derived from URL hash on load and hashchange)
  - editing: { id:number|null, draft:string } (ephemeral only)
- Operations (preconditions -> postconditions; all commit persist when storage.mode=='local'):
  - add(title)
    - pre: typeof title==='string'; let t=title.trim(); t.length>0
    - post: items := items ⊕ { id:nextId, title:t, completed:false }; nextId := nextId+1
    - invariants: ids remain unique; order is append-only aside from removals.
  - remove(id)
    - pre: ∃ i in items s.t. i.id===id
    - post: items := items \ { i | i.id===id }
  - setTitle(id, title)
    - pre: ∃ i in items; title is string
    - post: let t=title.trim(); if t==='' then remove(id) else items[id].title := t
  - setCompleted(id, bool)
    - pre: ∃ i in items; typeof bool==='boolean'
    - post: items[id].completed := bool
  - setAllCompleted(bool)
    - pre: typeof bool==='boolean'
    - post: ∀i in items, i.completed := bool (regardless of current route)
  - clearCompleted()
    - post: items := { i in items | !i.completed }
  - routeTo(kind)
    - pre: kind in {'all','active','completed'}
    - post: location.hash := '#/'+kind (hash is the source of truth); state.route := kind
  - beginEdit(id)
    - pre: ∃ i in items
    - post: editing := { id, draft: items[id].title }
  - commitEdit()
    - pre: editing.id !== null
    - post: setTitle(editing.id, editing.draft); editing := {id:null, draft:''}
  - cancelEdit()
    - post: editing := {id:null, draft:''} (no item changes)
Derived view and controls:
- .todo-list reflects items filtered by route: all, active(!completed), completed.
- Per-li DOM: li[data-id] has class 'completed' iff item.completed; contains input.toggle (if enabled), label (double-click to edit), button.destroy; input.edit shown only when li has class editing.
- #toggle-all reflects collection: checked iff items.length>0 and all items completed; toggling it sets ALL items completed to its state, even when a filter hides some.
- .todo-count strong shows count of all active items (not just visible); updates on any mutation.
- .clear-completed hidden if no completed items; clicking removes all completed.
- .filters anchors #/, #/active, #/completed; 'selected' class tracks route; filtering updates immediately on route or data changes; hash survives reload.
Persistence (if enabled):
- localStorage key: todos-transfer; after every committed mutation add/remove/toggle/edit/setAll/clear, write JSON: [{id,title,completed}]. On load, restore array, discard invalid entries; compute nextId := 1 + max(id) or 1 when empty. Editing state is never saved.
Limitations:
- Re-render replaces list content on each mutation; during an edit session, only explicit commit/cancel triggers render, so typed draft is not lost. Route changes during editing end the edit (cancel) to avoid draft/DOM mismatch.
- No network, no frameworks, single-document app. All labels and markup are frozen; plans only toggle semantics and capabilities.

libraries.design: A configurable TodoMVC-style checklist application. The library separates data management (todo items with identity, title, completed state), UI rendering (input, list, filters, controls), persistence (localStorage), and routing (hash-based filtering). Components include: item creation with trimming/validation, inline editing with commit/cancel, toggle individual/all items, filter views (all/active/completed), clear completed items, and localStorage persistence. The design uses a capability-based configuration where features can be independently enabled.

libraries.design: A composable todo-list library with pluggable state management, UI rendering, and persistence. Core abstractions: (1) TodoStore - manages item identity, title, and completion state with immutable updates; (2) ViewFilter - computes visible subsets based on completion status; (3) EditSession - tracks in-progress edits with cancel/commit semantics; (4) PersistenceAdapter - serializes/deserializes store snapshots; (5) Router - maps URL hash to filter state. State ownership: TodoStore owns canonical item collection, EditSession owns transient edit state, Router owns filter selection. Operations are pure functions returning new state plus side-effect descriptions. UI layer binds DOM events to operations and renders derived views. Identity invariant: each item has a unique numeric ID assigned at creation. Derived-view consistency: filter membership and aggregate counts recompute on every state change.

Reusable full-page GUI library: KeyedTableUI. Components: 1) Toolbar with fixed public controls by id: #run, #runlots, #add, #update, #clear, #swaprows. Buttons are optionally included by configuration but keep their public ids when present. 2) Keyed table:
. Each row is a persistent keyed tr with data-id equal to its numeric ID; td 1 shows the ID, td 2 holds an a label, td 3 holds an a.remove for removal. Selection is indicated by class danger on the tr. 3) State model in browser memory: rows[] = [{id, label}], idToRow: Map(id->tr), selectedId: number|null, nextId: number. Contract: for every surviving row identity (ID), its DOM tr instance is retained across updates, selection changes, removals of other rows, appends and reordering; only replace on explicit replace operations (run/runlots). IDs are strictly increasing within the page session and never reused, across all operations including clear and replace. 4) Event delegation on tbody for clicks on label anchors (select) and a.remove anchors (remove), ensuring minimal DOM churn. 5) Operations: run replaces with 1000 new rows; runlots replaces with 10000 new rows; add appends 1000 new rows; update appends literal " !!!" to labels at positions 0,10,20,...; clear removes all rows and clears selection; swaprows exchanges rows at indices 1 and 998 when length >= 999. Selection persists by identity through appends, updates and reorders; selection is cleared on replace/clear or when the selected row is removed. 6) Composition surface: a data-only plan configures which controls render, their order, visual theme, table density, and counts for run/runlots. The compiler resolves defaults and emits a complete static site: index.html, style, and an ES module runtime. Limitations: labels are fixed as "Row N" for ID N; no networking or frameworks; counts and features can be narrowed but public ids and semantics are fixed when features are enabled.

libraries.design:
Overview
- This package compiles a full-page static site that renders a high-performance keyed table with deterministic operations. It is built around composable operations over a single authoritative state and a keyed DOM reconciler that preserves row node identity across updates, appends, removals, and reordering.

State ownership
- Model state (owned by the Store):
  - rows: ordered array of { id:number, label:string }
  - selectedId: number|null
  - nextId: number (monotonically increasing; never decreases or repeats during the page session)
- View state (owned by the View):
  - idToNode: Map<number, HTMLTableRowElement> mapping data identity to the DOM row node. This is derived from model state and may be rebuilt; it does not define truth.

Identity invariants
- Row identity is the row.id value. It is globally unique and strictly increasing over time during the page session.
- The same tr DOM node is retained for every surviving row.id across appends, updates, selection changes, removals, replaces, and reorders. Removed or replaced ids lose their nodes.
- tbody child order exactly matches the order of model.rows.

Operations (pure, composable)
- All operations are pure functions State -> State, usable in any composition.
- reset(count): Replace rows with count fresh rows using new unique ids; clears selection; advances nextId by count.
- append(count): Append count fresh rows using new unique ids; keeps selection.
- clear(): Set rows to empty; clears selection; nextId unchanged.
- updateEvery10(): For rows at indices 0,10,20,... append literal " !!!" to label; selection unchanged.
- select(id): Set selectedId = id.
- remove(id): Remove only the row with this id; if it was selected, clear selection; other order preserved.
- swap(): If at least 999 rows, swap positions 1 and 998; otherwise no-op; selection follows id.

Operation preconditions and postconditions
- reset(count>=0)
  - Pre: count is a non-negative integer. No other requirements.
  - Post: rows.length === count; every new row has label exactly "Row N" for its id N; selectedId === null; nextId increased by count; no previous ids survive.
- append(count>=0)
  - Pre: count is a non-negative integer.
  - Post: rows length increases by count; appended labels exactly "Row N"; selection unchanged; nextId increased by count.
- clear()
  - Pre: none.
  - Post: rows empty; selectedId null; nextId unchanged.
- updateEvery10()
  - Pre: none.
  - Post: For each i in [0..rows.length) where i%10===0, rows[i].label gains a trailing " !!!"; repeated calls repeat the suffixing; identities and order unchanged.
- select(id)
  - Pre: id exists in rows.
  - Post: selectedId === id; order and labels unchanged.
- remove(id)
  - Pre: id exists in rows.
  - Post: Exactly that id removed; other rows keep their relative order; if selectedId===id then selectedId becomes null; otherwise unchanged.
- swap()
  - Pre: rows.length >= 999.
  - Post: rows[1] and rows[998] swapped; identities preserved; selection by id preserved.

Derived-view consistency
- Reconciler enforces:
  - For each row in model.rows, there is exactly one tr[data-id="id"].
  - The index of each tr equals its row's index.
  - td1 text equals id; td2 contains an a with the label; td3 contains an a.remove for removal; selected row has class danger.
- Selection styling is derived from selectedId and applied per-row without re-creating nodes.

Limitations
- Single table per page instance.
- Intended for up to tens of thousands of rows; operations are O(n) with small constant factors.
- No virtual scrolling; DOM size equals row count.

Reuse
- The core store and keyed reconciler are generic utilities. The same operations can be recomposed or extended for new capabilities without changing the reconciler or DOM contract.

Configuration controls which buttons and interactions are enabled.

libraries.design: A reusable keyed table library with composable state operations. The core abstraction is a keyed collection where each row has a stable numeric ID and mutable label. Operations maintain DOM node identity for surviving IDs across all mutations. State ownership: a single array of {id, label} objects is the source of truth; a Map tracks id->DOM node bindings; selectedId tracks selection. Operations are pure transforms on data plus imperative DOM sync. Capabilities are orthogonal features (update-in-place, selection, removal, swapping) that compose without interference. The library provides: createTable(container, capabilities) returning an operation interface; operations like replaceRows(count), appendRows(count), updateEveryNth(n, suffix), selectById(id), removeById(id), swapIndices(i, j), clear(). Each operation updates state, then reconciles DOM using the id->node map to reuse nodes. ID generation is monotonic across all operations. Selection follows data identity through all transforms.

limitations: Two familiar source applications, one seed per builder/planner; no independent-project significance claim.
Construction comparison is a prompt-level process contrast, not a new learned abstraction algorithm.
Development exposes primitive semantics and UI selectors; heldout trajectories are unseen, not all semantic information.
Full-merge is a deterministic deployable control; success of any subset merge is only a finite-set reachable witness.
Extra unrequested working features were allowed; fixed development examples may already implement the full target.
